theory.intro: A composite shape here is built from straight edges and one or more arcs. Its perimeter is the total distance around the **outside boundary**, so it is the sum of the straight sections plus the length of every arc on the boundary. Any edge inside the shape, such as a diameter that an arc has replaced, is not counted.
facts: Only edges on the outside boundary count. A dashed construction line drawn inside the shape is not part of the perimeter.
A semicircular arc of diameter $d$ has length $\frac{1}{2}\times \pi d$; the diameter itself is not counted when the arc replaces it.
A quarter-circle arc of radius $r$ has length $\frac{1}{4}\times 2\pi r$.
For any other arc, $l = \frac{\theta}{360}\times 2\pi r$, where $\theta$ is the angle at the centre.
$P = l + 2r$ applies to a sector only. A shape with straight edges that are not both radii needs each boundary piece added separately.
steps: Label every length on the perimeter.
Add the straight sections and the arc lengths.

foundation.solution_text:
$P = l + 2r$ is the perimeter of a **sector**, whose only straight edges are two radii meeting at the centre.
This shape is not a sector: its straight edges are three sides of a rectangle.
The perimeter is made of the bottom $6$ cm, the two sides of $3$ cm each, and the semicircular arc of diameter $6$ cm.

The two semicircular ends each have diameter $12$ m, so together they make one whole circle.
$P = 20 + 20 + \pi(12)$
$= 77.7\text{ m}$

development.solution_text:
Each of the four arcs is a semicircle of diameter $5$ cm.
$P = 4\times \frac{1}{2}\times \pi(5)$
$= 10\pi\text{ cm}$

The two semicircular ends have the same radius, so together they make one whole circle.
$P = 84.4 + 84.4 + 2\pi(36.5)$
$= 398.14\text{ m}$

mastery.solution_text:
1. **Label every length on the perimeter.**
The boundary is two lengths of $x$, the $6$ cm end, and a semicircular arc of diameter $6$ cm.
2. **Add the straight sections and the arc lengths.**
$P = 2x + 6 + \frac{1}{2}\times \pi(6)$
3. **Calculate and round as required.**
$30 = 2x + 6 + 9.4247\ldots$
$2x = 14.5752\ldots$
$x = 7.29\text{ cm}$

Shape A: $P = 4\times 10$
$= 40\text{ cm}$
Shape B: the two semicircular ends have diameter $6$ cm, so together they make one whole circle.
$P = 10 + 10 + \pi(6)$
$= 38.8495\ldots\text{ cm}$
Shape A is larger by $40 - 38.8495\ldots = 1.15\text{ cm}$.
